_about.purpose: Curated decisions applied on top of the original draft (data/atlas_v2.json), which is kept untouched for provenance.
_about.rule: Every correction records who decided it, why, and where the replacement came from. Gene symbols introduced here are resolved by the pipeline like any other — a correction is an instruction, never a verification.
_about.pinning_note: Where a gene family could not be pinned to a named ortholog in the stated crop, it is listed in unpinned[] rather than replaced by a guess.
_about.alias_note: search_aliases map a literature symbol to the symbol NCBI actually indexes. They widen the search; they never assert the genes are the same — the pipeline still has to find a record, and the corroboration used here is chromosome agreement with the locus ID.
_about.locus_identity_note: gene_locus ties a literature symbol to its genome locus tag. When NCBI Gene holds no record for the symbol, the pipeline resolves identity from the GenBank record that carries that locus_tag, reading /product and /protein_id off the record itself.
_about.accession_note: gene_accession pins a symbol to a specific GenBank record when neither NCBI Gene nor a locus tag resolves it. The pipeline fetches the record and reads its organism, gene name and product, so a wrong accession fails loudly instead of being trusted.
_about.id_note: gene_ncbi_id pins a symbol to an NCBI Gene record by ID. The pipeline fetches the record and checks the organism, so a wrong ID fails loudly.
_about.commercial_rule: Level 1 means THIS entry's genetic solution is in a commercial product — not that a product exists with the same trait by another route. commercial_product is set only when a source ties the named product to the entry's gene or allele.

EGG-PRICKLE-01.decision: Replace the draft's SmMYB candidates with SmLOG1 as the gene, keeping SmMYB recorded as a superseded candidate.
EGG-PRICKLE-01.rationale: PMID 38974191 fine-mapped the PE locus on chromosome 6 to a 9233 bp interval holding one candidate, SmLOG1, a LONELY GUY family cytokinin biosynthetic enzyme, and CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of it abolished prickles in all tissues. The draft's SmMYB candidates are a different gene and that paper does not support them.

set.gene_function: LONELY GUY (LOG) family cytokinin biosynthetic enzyme; expressed mainly in immature prickles.
set.editing_possibility: Promoter editing, or marker-assisted selection on the CAPS marker at -735 bp: the causal variation reported is non-coding, so a coding knockout is not the route the natural prickleless allele uses.
set.trait_inheritance: Single dominant nuclear gene (PE locus, chromosome 6)

superseded.why: Not supported by PMID 38974191. Kept here so the earlier hypothesis is not silently erased; if another source supports an SmMYB role, it can return as its own entry.

EGG-PRICKLE-01.second_suggestion_note: A later suggestion attributed PMID 38974191 to 'Satterlee et al., 2024, Science'. That is wrong and contradicts the same supplier's earlier, correct attribution: the paper is Zhang L, Horticulture Research 2024. It also offered the locus tag SMEL4.1_06g011220.1.01, which cannot be checked here because eggplant has no NCBI build.

GAP-COMB-01.decision: Pin the gene families to named tomato orthologs so the entry stops naming families as if they were targets. Tomato chosen as the reference crop because it is the best annotated of the three the draft listed.
GAP-COMB-01.rationale: Symbols resolved by querying NCBI Gene for Solanum lycopersicum.
unpinned: HKT1;2 — no gene of that name is annotated for Solanum lycopersicum in NCBI Gene. The draft's HKT1;2 claim most likely refers to SlHKT1;2 from the S. pennellii introgression literature, which is a different (cisgenic) route and should become its own entry rather than part of this network.

GAP-REPRO-01.decision: Pin to named tomato orthologs; keep the unpinnable part explicit.
GAP-REPRO-01.rationale: Symbols resolved by querying NCBI Gene for Solanum lycopersicum.
unpinned: ROS scavengers — a functional class, not a gene; APX1 above is one member and stands for itself.
MADS-box regulators — too generic to pin; needs a specific gene before it can be an entry.

GAP-RECOV-01.decision: Pin what resolves; leave the rest as an open research question rather than an entry.
GAP-RECOV-01.rationale: Symbols resolved by querying NCBI Gene for Solanum lycopersicum.
unpinned: WOX, PLT (PLETHORA), LBD, DRO1 — none are annotated under those names for Solanum lycopersicum in NCBI Gene. Root-architecture work in tomato uses different symbols; until one is named, post-stress root recovery stays a research question, not an atlas target.

TOM-VITD-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
TOM-VITD-01.decision: Keep Sl7-DR2 as the literature symbol and search NCBI under DWF5-2, the symbol it indexes.
TOM-VITD-01.rationale: The suggestion's NCBI id LOC101268773 is wrong: that record is 'protein YIP4b-like' on chromosome 7 and has nothing to do with sterols. The tomato 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase in NCBI Gene is DWF5-2 (101256596) on chromosome 6, which agrees with the claimed locus Solyc06g074090 being a chromosome-6 tag. A second 7-DHC reductase exists on chromosome 1 (LOC101248602), so the chromosome match is corroboration, not proof: confirm against the paper before calling it settled.

TOM-TOBRFV-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
TOM-TOBRFV-01.decision: Search the TOM genes under the older GenBank symbols NCBI indexes: LeTH3/TH3 and LeTH1/TH1.
TOM-TOBRFV-01.rationale: Confirmed in NCBI: TH3 (778361, alias LeTH3) is 'tobamovirus multiplication 1 homolog 3' on chromosome 2, and TH1 (778313, alias LeTH1) is 'tobamovirus multiplication 1 homolog' on chromosome 4. Both RefSeq proteins given in the suggestion check out: NP_001234306.1 is homolog 3 and NP_001234096.1 is homolog. The chromosomes agree with the suggested loci (SlTOM1a = Solyc02g080370 on chr2, SlTOM3 = Solyc04g008540 on chr4), which means the NCBI names run opposite to the paper's: the gene the paper calls SlTOM1a is indexed as homolog 3. Anyone editing these must key on the locus tag, not the number in the symbol.

CUC-BITTER-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
CUC-BITTER-01.decision: Resolve the three bitterness genes by their GenBank records rather than NCBI Gene symbols.
CUC-BITTER-01.rationale: The suggestion's NCBI ids for Bt and Bl are wrong genes: LOC101214378 is 'UPF0307 protein ECA0281' on chromosome 3 and LOC101214672 is a leucine-rich repeat extensin on chromosome 5. The loci themselves do resolve, in GenBank, with the locus tag on the record: Csa5G157230 = KM655852, bHLH transcription factor, protein AIT72027.1 (Bt); Csa5G156220 = KM655851, bHLH transcription factor, AIT72026.1 (Bl); Csa6G088690 = KM655855, oxidosqualene cyclase, AIT72030.1 (Bi). The cucurbitadienol synthase in NCBI Gene (LOC101204533, chromosome 6) agrees with Bi's chromosome.

locus_identity.Bt (Csa5G157230): GenBank KM655852, bHLH transcription factor, protein AIT72027.1
locus_identity.Bl (Csa5G156220): GenBank KM655851, bHLH transcription factor, protein AIT72026.1
locus_identity.Bi (Csa6G088690): GenBank KM655855, oxidosqualene cyclase, protein AIT72030.1

CUC-BITTER-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1. 'Marketmore' and 'Spacemaster' are long-standing cucumber cultivars, and the claim that they were 'engineered or selected' for tissue-specific bitterness regulation conflates ordinary non-bitter fruit with the Bt/Bl regulatory solution described in PMID 25430763. Non-bitter fruit in cucumber predates that work by decades.

TOM-TYLCV-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
TOM-TYLCV-01.decision: Search SlPelo under PELOTA, the symbol NCBI indexes.
TOM-TYLCV-01.rationale: Confirmed: NCBI Gene 101251671 is PELOTA, 'protein pelota homolog', chromosome 4 of Solanum lycopersicum, and NM_001279230.1 is its mRNA — both exactly as suggested. Chromosome 4 agrees with the suggested locus Solyc04g009810. One correction to the suggestion: the paper is in PLoS Genetics, not Plant Cell; first author Lapidot M, 2015, as claimed.
TOM-TYLCV-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1. The cultivar names offered — 'Camaro', 'Grand Marshall', 'Jolene' — were not confirmed, and the claim mixed introgressed natural ty-5 alleles with targeted modifications, which are different routes. ty-5 resistance is widely deployed commercially; what is missing is a source naming a cultivar and its ty-5/Pelota allele.

PEP-MILDEW-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
PEP-MILDEW-01.decision: Fix the truncated gene string and search under the symbols NCBI indexes, MLO1 and MLO2.
PEP-MILDEW-01.rationale: The draft's gene field read 'CaMLO2 (CaMLO family)', which the parser turned into a stray fragment. The paper (PLoS One 2013, first author Zheng Z, as claimed) tested CaMlo1 and CaMlo2 by VIGS. Confirmed in NCBI for Capsicum annuum: LOC107871340, 'MLO-like protein 12', alias MLO2; and LOC107848305, 'MLO-like protein 6', alias MLO1.

WAT-BRIX-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
WAT-BRIX-01.decision: Narrow this entry to ClTST2 and move ClSWEET3 and ClLCYB out of it.
WAT-BRIX-01.rationale: PMID 29118248 (Plant Physiol 2018, first author Ren Y, 'A Tonoplast Sugar Transporter Underlies a Sugar Accumulation QTL in Watermelon') characterises ClTST2 and its upstream regulator, not ClSWEET3 or ClLCYB — so the draft bundled three genes under one paper that covers one of them. Flesh colour (ClLCYB) is a different trait from sugar accumulation and should never have shared an entry with it. Two corrections to the suggestion: the accession it gave for ClTST2, MF497324, is a Marquandomyces marquandii fungal ITS sequence, not watermelon; the real record is KY367352.1, /gene=TST2, product 'tonoplast sugar transporter 2', protein ATQ36703.1. And Citrullus lanatus does have NCBI Gene records (185 of them), though none is named TST, SWEET or LCYB, so the practical conclusion stands: identity has to come from GenBank.

superseded.why: Not characterised in PMID 29118248. ClSWEET3 needs its own entry and its own paper; ClLCYB is flesh colour, a separate trait. Removed here rather than left implying evidence they do not have.

LET-VITC-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
LET-VITC-01.decision: Drop uORF from the gene field and pin LsGGP2 to its real NCBI record.
LET-VITC-01.rationale: uORF is a 5' UTR feature, not a gene — the suggestion was right about that. But its gene ID was wrong: 111882405 is EDR1, 'Protein kinase superfamily protein', in Lactuca sativa. The real record is LOC111907963, 'GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase 2', chromosome 7. A related gene, VTC5 (111899617), is also a GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase, so confirm against the paper which one was edited. PMID 30080209 is confirmed: Zhang H, Nat Biotechnol 2018, uORF editing for translational control.

BRA-CLUB-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
BRA-CLUB-01.decision: Narrow the entry to CRa, anchored to GenBank AB751517.
BRA-CLUB-01.rationale: PMID 23054353 is confirmed: Ueno H, Plant Mol Biol 2012, 'Molecular characterization of the CRa gene conferring clubroot resistance', and AB751517.1 is confirmed as Brassica rapa subsp. pekinensis CRa mRNA for a putative disease resistance protein. The paper covers CRa only, so CRb, Crr1 and Crr3 do not belong in this entry. The suggestion's NCBI gene ID 103860516 is not usable: that record is 'uncharacterized LOC103860516', not the TMV-resistance-like protein described, so identity comes from the accession instead.

superseded.why: Not characterised in PMID 23054353. The PMIDs offered for them were checked and are wrong papers entirely: 23175754 is about cellulose microfibrils in collenchyma, and 24831572 is a cardiovascular medicine review. Each locus needs its own entry and a real reference.

BRA-CLUB-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1. The literature does document that CR loci have been introduced into commercial F1 cultivars of Chinese cabbage, and that CRb/CRbKato is the same allele as CRa (Breeding Science 72:21040; Hatakeyama et al. 2017), and Syngenta holds a patent on monogenic dominant clubroot resistance introgressed into B. oleracea. But the specific cultivar names offered — Kilaton F1, Clapton F1, Crispus F1, Monclano F1 — could not be tied to CRa by any source found, and 'carries a major CR locus' is not the same claim as 'carries this gene'. Needs one source naming a cultivar and its locus.

ONI-TEAR-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
ONI-TEAR-01.decision: Narrow the entry to LFS, anchored to GenBank AB089203.
ONI-TEAR-01.rationale: AB089203.1 is confirmed as Allium cepa lfs mRNA for lachrymatory factor synthase, and Allium cepa has no NCBI Gene build, so the accession is the identity anchor. PMID 18583530 silences LFS by RNAi; it does not test AcACS1 or AcACS2, so those leave this entry.

superseded.why: Not tested in PMID 18583530. Onion pungency via ACS genes is a separate trait needing its own entry and reference.

ONI-TEAR-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1, and this is the clearest case of why the rule matters. Sunions is a real marketed tearless onion from BASF/Nunhems, but BASF states it is the result of more than three decades of CONVENTIONAL breeding, with pungency tracked by pyruvic acid measurement. This entry's solution is RNAi silencing of LFS (PMID 18583530). Same trait, different genetic route: the product does not validate the entry's solution, so Level 1 would be a false claim.

EGG-BROWN-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13, from an external AI suggestion (Gemini) checked against NCBI
EGG-BROWN-01.decision: Use the paper's four-letter prefix (SmelPPO4/5/6) and leave identity unresolved for now.
EGG-BROWN-01.rationale: PMID 33343607 is confirmed: Maioli A, Front Plant Sci 2020, 'Simultaneous CRISPR/Cas9 Editing of Three PPO Genes Reduces Fruit Flesh Browning'. Solanum melongena has no NCBI Gene build, as the suggestion said. But the three GenBank accessions it offered are not eggplant PPO genes at all: AY547272 is a Pseudomonas fluorescens rsmE gene, AY547273 is a tomato early light inducible protein, and AY547274 is a Leptosphaeria maculans actin gene. NCBI's eggplant PPO records are for PPO10, not PPO4/5/6, so the SMEL_008g3125xx tags need the eggplant genome database, which this environment cannot reach. Identity therefore stays unresolved rather than anchored to a wrong record.
unpinned: SMEL_008g312510 / 312500 / 312490 — eggplant genome tags, not resolvable from NCBI.

TOM-GABA-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13; product claim relayed from Gemini and checked on the web
TOM-GABA-01.decision: Set Level 1: the entry's own solution is the commercial product.
TOM-GABA-01.rationale: Sanatech Seed's 'Sicilian Rouge High GABA' has been sold to consumers in Japan since September 2021 and is reported as the first commercially sold CRISPR-edited food. The edit is CRISPR/Cas9 on tomato GAD disabling the C-terminal autoinhibitory/calmodulin-binding domain, which is exactly this entry's mechanism, and the fruit carries about 4-6x the GABA of unedited controls. Sources: Nature Biotechnology news (d41587-021-00026-2), Scientific American, and a Philippine regulatory product information sheet naming Sanatech Seed and the GAD target.

set.commercial_product: Sicilian Rouge High GABA (Sanatech Seed, Japan, retail since Sept 2021) — CRISPR/Cas9 edit of GAD, the same mechanism as this entry

BRA-GLUC-01.decided_by: maintainer, 2026-11-13; product claim relayed from Gemini and checked on the web
BRA-GLUC-01.decision: Set Level 1: the commercialised hybrids carry the allele this entry names.
BRA-GLUC-01.rationale: Traka et al., New Phytologist 2013 (doi 10.1111/nph.12232) reports that two high-glucoraphanin F1 hybrids were commercialised as Beneforte broccoli and that all of them carry an introgressed Brassica villosa segment containing a B. villosa Myb28 allele, with 2.5-3x the glucoraphanin of standard hybrids. The product and the entry's gene are the same thing. Note this is an introgression from a crossable wild relative, so the route is cisgenic, not a native edit.

set.commercial_product: Beneforte broccoli (two commercialised F1 hybrids) — carry an introgressed B. villosa Myb28 allele, this entry's gene

PEP-PUNG-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1 by the pipeline, and worth a human decision. Every commercial sweet bell pepper is pun1 loss-of-function, so the allele is commercially ubiquitous — but it arrived through domestication centuries ago, not through this solution being deployed. The cultivars offered ('Ace', 'Bell Boy') illustrate the allele rather than validate a breeding route. If Level 1 is meant to say 'this allele is in commercial products', this qualifies; if it means 'this solution was deployed commercially', it does not.

PEP-VIRUS-01.commercial_status: NOT set to Level 1: no cultivar was named, only 'commercial hybrid lines bred with pvr1/pvr2' and a list of seed companies. A category is not a product.
